<cell id="b664eeac"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type># Genre Operational Synergy

The investment firm wants to identify which game genres have the strongest operational synergy based on publisher portfolios.</cell id="b664eeac">
<cell id="f176d7e8"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Load and prepare the data

Load the Steam dataset and prepare the publisher and genre information needed to represent publisher portfolios.</cell id="f176d7e8">
<cell id="3aa36c4f">import numpy as np
import pandas as pd


STEAM_PATH = "../../data/steam/steam.csv"

GENRES = [
    "Action",
    "Adventure",
    "Casual",
    "Indie",
    "RPG",
    "Strategy",
    "Simulation",
    "Sports",
]

steam = pd.read_csv(STEAM_PATH)

print(
    "Dataset loaded:",
    f"{len(steam):,} games",
)

<cell id="44793ea7"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Prepare publisher–genre assignments

Expand games with multiple genre or publisher labels so each publisher's activity can be summarized separately within each genre.</cell id="44793ea7">
<cell id="1f54991a">data = (
    steam.assign(
        genre=steam["genres"]
        .fillna("")
        .str.split(";"),
        publisher_name=steam["publisher"]
        .fillna("")
        .str.split(";"),
    )
    .explode("genre")
    .explode("publisher_name")
)

data["genre"] = (
    data["genre"]
    .str.strip()
)

data["publisher_name"] = (
    data["publisher_name"]
    .str.strip()
)

data = data[
    data["genre"].isin(GENRES)
    & data["publisher_name"].ne("")
].drop_duplicates(
    [
        "appid",
        "publisher_name",
        "genre",
    ]
)


print(
    "Games represented:",
    f"{data['appid'].nunique():,}",
)

print(
    "Publishers represented:",
    f"{data['publisher_name'].nunique():,}",
)

print(
    "Publisher–genre assignments:",
    f"{len(data):,}",
)</cell id="1f54991a">

<cell id="29e83bd7"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Represent publisher portfolios

Use publisher title counts to represent operational activity within each genre.

Genres with similar publisher title-count distributions are treated as having stronger operational synergy.</cell id="29e83bd7">
<cell id="6e2aaff1">title_matrix = (
    data
    .groupby(
        [
            "publisher_name",
            "genre",
        ]
    )["appid"]
    .nunique()
    .unstack(fill_value=0)
    .reindex(
        columns=GENRES,
        fill_value=0,
    )
)


print(
    "Publisher portfolios:",
    f"{len(title_matrix):,} publishers × "
    f"{len(title_matrix.columns)} genres",
)

print(
    "Portfolio measure:",
    "publisher title counts",
)</cell id="6e2aaff1">

Publisher portfolios: 14,044 publishers × 8 genres
Portfolio measure: publisher title counts

<cell id="c18a120f"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Calculate genre synergy

Calculate cosine similarity between publisher title-count portfolios and identify the genre pair with the highest similarity.</cell id="c18a120f">
<cell id="0d837e3d">x = title_matrix.to_numpy()

similarity = (
    x.T @ x
) / np.outer(
    np.linalg.norm(x, axis=0),
    np.linalg.norm(x, axis=0),
)

np.fill_diagonal(
    similarity,
    np.nan,
)


i, j = np.unravel_index(
    np.nanargmax(similarity),
    similarity.shape,
)

genre_1 = GENRES[i]
genre_2 = GENRES[j]
score = similarity[i, j]


print(
    "Strongest genre pair:",
    f"{genre_1} + {genre_2}",
)

print(
    "Synergy score:",
    f"{score:.3f}",
)</cell id="0d837e3d">

Strongest genre pair: Adventure + Casual
Synergy score: 0.724

<cell id="5f24feb8"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Visualize the result

Visualize the strongest genre pair and its similarity score.</cell id="5f24feb8">
<cell id="d797ed20">import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


label = f"{genre_1} + {genre_2}"

fig, ax = plt.subplots(
    figsize=(8, 5)
)

bar = ax.bar(
    [label],
    [score],
)

ax.set_title(
    "Strongest Genre Synergy"
)

ax.set_ylabel(
    "Synergy Score"
)

ax.set_ylim(0, 1)

ax.text(
    bar[0].get_x() + bar[0].get_width() / 2,
    score,
    f"{score:.3f}",
    ha="center",
    va="bottom",
)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()</cell id="d797ed20">
